studies.Population: NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study participants aged 50–71 years
studies.Smoking Status: Never smokers, former smokers, and current smokers; multivariable models adjusted for detailed smoking categories
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Meat and components of meat and the risk of bladder cancer in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.
studies.Authors: Ferrucci LM, Sinha R, Ward MH, Graubard BI, Hollenbeck AR, Kilfoy BA, Schatzkin A, Michaud DS, Cross AJ
studies.Timing: Baseline dietary assessment in 1995–1996 with 7 years of follow-up
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: At baseline, participants completed a 124-item food frequency questionnaire

sample_size.excerpt: During 7 years of follow-up, 854 transitional cell bladder-cancer cases were identified among 300,933 men and women who had completed a validated food-frequency questionnaire in the large prospective NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.

cases.excerpt: During 7 years of follow-up, 854 transitional cell bladder-cancer cases were identified among 300,933 men and women who had completed a validated food-frequency questionnaire in the large prospective NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.

effect_size.excerpt: The hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for red meat (HR for fifth quintile compared with first quintile, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.96-1.54; P(trend) = .07) and the HCA 2-amino-1 methyl-6-phenylimidazo(4,5-b)pyridine (PhIP) (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.95-1.48; P(trend) = .06) conferred a borderline statistically significant increased risk of bladder cancer.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for red meat (HR for fifth quintile compared with first quintile, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.96-1.54; P(trend) = .07) and the HCA 2-amino-1 methyl-6-phenylimidazo(4,5-b)pyridine (PhIP) (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.95-1.48; P(trend) = .06) conferred a borderline statistically significant increased risk of bladder cancer.

p_value.excerpt: red meat (HR for fifth quintile compared with first quintile, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.96-1.54; P(trend) = .07)

comparison.excerpt: the lowest quantile served as the referent; although quintiles were used for most variables

design.excerpt: Cases included transitional cell bladder cancer with codes C67.0–C67.9, encompassing morphologies 8050, 8120–8122, and 8130
design.location: Methods, Identification of cases and cohort follow-up

timing.excerpt: During 7 years of follow-up, 854 transitional cell bladder cancer cases were identified

exposure_measurement.excerpt: At baseline, participants completed a 124-item food frequency questionnaire

gender.excerpt: Our analytic cohort consisted of 300,933 persons; 125,574 women and 175,359 men
